page.text:
A basis is a subset $B \subseteq V$ that is simultaneously linearly
independent and spans $V$. Equivalently, every vector $v \in V$ admits a
*unique* expression as a finite linear combination of basis vectors:
$$ v = \sum_{b \in B} c_b b, $$ where all but finitely many scalars
$c_b \in F$ are zero. The requirement of finiteness ensures that
algebraic sums remain strictly well-defined even when the basis $B$ is
uncountably infinite.
